content.identity:
### Plasma-Wall Interaction Group - Members and Affiliation

The KTH Plasma-Wall Interaction (PWI) group is hosted by the Department of Electromagnetics and Plasma Physics (EMP), School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, KTH Royal Institute of Technology. The official group page lists three named members.

| Name | Role at KTH | Department | Public email | Profile URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marek Rubel | Professor Emeritus | Electromagnetics & Plasma Physics | rubel@kth.se | https://www.kth.se/profile/rubel?l=en |
| Henrik Bergsaker | Associate Professor | Electromagnetics & Plasma Physics | henricb@kth.se | https://www.kth.se/profile/henricb?l=en |
| Per Petersson | Researcher | Electromagnetics & Plasma Physics | ppeter@kth.se | https://www.kth.se/profile/ppetter?l=en |

Source: https://www.kth.se/emp/research/fusion/plasma-wall-interaction-pwi-1.37584 (group roster section, last changed Jan 15, 2026).

### Research Scope of the PWI Group

The group's stated strategic goal is "to carry out a strong experimentally-based program focused on ITER-relevant topics", covering:
- Lifetime of plasma-facing materials (PFM) and plasma-facing components (PFC)
- Tritium inventory accumulation in PFC
- Carbon and metal (Be, W) dust formation
- Material migration studies via tracer techniques and in-vessel diagnostics
- Development of fuel removal methods (photonic cleaning, laser, ICWC/ECWC)
- Surface analysis of plasma-facing components (nuclear microprobe, IBA)

The page lists routine participation in EUROfusion, ITPA, IEA, and IUVSTA frameworks, with collaborators at JET/UK, CEA Cadarache (WEST), Max-Planck IPP Garching, Forschungszentrum Julich (TOMAS), Uppsala University (ion beam analysis), and Czech Academy COMPASS tokamak.

Source: https://www.kth.se/emp/research/fusion/plasma-wall-interaction-pwi-1.37584

### Adjacent Fusion Groups at KTH EMP (Disambiguation)

The wider KTH fusion portfolio includes groups whose topics can overlap PWI but are distinct. The Five-Sub-Group Map below clarifies the scope and avoids merging namesakes.

| Group | Primary Focus | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Plasma-Wall Interaction (PWI) | Erosion/deposition, dust, tritium inventory, diagnostics | https://www.kth.se/emp/research/fusion/plasma-wall-interaction-pwi-1.37584 |
| Pedestal Physics | High-confinement-mode pedestal behavior | https://www.kth.se/emp/research/fusion |
| Plasma Control | Plasma control systems | https://www.kth.se/emp/research/fusion |
| Heating and Current Drive | ICRF heating, magnetohydrodynamic control | https://www.kth.se/emp/research/fusion |
| Fusion Plasma Device | EXTRAP T2R reversed-field pinch device | https://www.kth.se/emp/research/fusion/extrap-1.897096 |
| Fast Electron Physics | Fast-electron transport | https://www.kth.se/emp/research/fusion/fast-electron-physics-1.1472187 |

Takeaway: lead-054 matches specifically the PWI sub-group; any hires or grants associated with Pedestal Physics, Plasma Control, Heating & Current Drive, EXTRAP T2R, or Fast Electron Physics are NOT part of PWI even if the umbrella "fusion research group" is the same department.

### Closely Affiliated Faculty on the PWI Topic

Svetlana Ratynskaia (Professor, KTH EMP) is shown leading work on dust formation in plasmas and runaway-electron-induced PFC damage - direct PWI-adjacent research. She is a Professor with email srat@kth.se and is one of the 36 KTH VR grantees (Nov 3, 2025 cycle). She teaches Applied Plasma Physics (EF2270) and Plasma Physics II (EF2215) at KTH.

Sources:
- https://www.kth.se/profile/srat?l=en
- https://www.kth.se/en/om/nyheter/centrala-nyheter/kth-forskare-far-155-miljoner-av-vetenskapsradet-1.1437168 (ratynskaia appears in funding list)
- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s41614-022-00081-5 (Ratynskaia, dust and powder in fusion plasmas)

content.synthesis_cross_cutting_insights:
### Showing the Perimeter of Evidence

The PWI roster at KTH (Rubel / Bergsaker / Petersson) is a small, publicly documented group whose recent competitive grants are not all surfaced through press-channel searches. The most clearly published 2025-2029 competitive award tied to PWI-adjacent research is Svetlana Ratynskaia's VR grant on explosive events in PFC. The KTH EMP's wider fusion cohort (Pedestal Physics, Plasma Control, H&CD, EXTRAP T2R, Fast Electron Physics) frames the scope: PWI is one of at least six fusion sub-groups, and any "fusion group" attribution should respect that separation.

### Distinguishing Funding Types (Apples to Oranges)

| Funding Type | Example for KTH PWI / EMP | Distinguishing Trait | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Competitive project grant | Ratynskaia VR "Explosive events..." 2025-2029 | Awarded through peer review of an open national call; PI-led | Quote funder, PI, period, scope |
| Consortium programme funding | Sweden - EUROfusion (Euratom GA 101052200) | Allocated by the consortium member (VR/Sweden) across programme work-packages | Flag as programme-level; do not attribute to a single PI |
| Institutional / faculty budget | KTH Doctoral student salary agreement | Used to hire doctoral students under a PI's allocation | Quote only if source explicitly ties funding to the PhD |
| Prize | None verified | Award for past accomplishment | Distinct from project grant |
| Doctoral hiring line | Embedded inside a PI's project or institution | Should not claim without explicit link | Avoid inferring |

Observation -> Mechanism -> Implication -> Recommendation: the only line where the available public evidence cleanly attributes a monetary grant is Ratynskaia's VR. -> For other PWI PIs, do not invent an amount or title.

### Confidence Ladder for Hiring

- Highest trust: official KTH vacancies index with category filter applied (https://www.kth.se/lediga-jobb?l=en?category=Doctoral+student etc.)
- Medium trust: EURAXESS
- Discovery only: LinkedIn / academic-positions mirrors (used to find candidate, not to confirm closure)

Recommendation: A re-run of this report in a future cycle should (1) drill into the KTH vacancies index filtered to "Doctoral student" + department "EMP" and (2) re-search VR's "Awarded grants" page for any grant where PI last name includes "Rubel", "Bergsaker", or "Petersson".
